signature.name: Römerberg
signature.detail: The historic heart of Frankfurt, a cobbled square framed by half-timbered houses and the city's iconic town hall. It is the most photographed spot in Frankfurt and a must-see for any first-time visitor. Tip: visit early morning to avoid crowds and get the best light for photos.

signature.name: Main Tower
signature.detail: One of Germany's tallest skyscrapers, offering an open-air observation deck with panoramic views over Frankfurt and the Rhine-Main region. It is a must for skyline lovers. Tip: go up about an hour before sunset to see the city in daylight and lit up at night; tickets are available at the entrance.

signature.name: Römer
signature.detail: Frankfurt's historic town hall, a medieval building that has served as the city's administrative center for centuries. Its distinctive facade is a symbol of the city. Tip: the inner courtyard is free to visit and less crowded than the square outside.

signature.name: Eiserner Steg
signature.detail: A pedestrian bridge over the Main River, famous for its love locks and views of the skyline. It is a romantic and practical crossing between the old town and Sachsenhausen. Tip: walk across at dusk for beautiful reflections of the city lights on the water.

signature.name: Goethe House
signature.detail: The birthplace of Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, now a museum dedicated to his life and work. It offers a glimpse into 18th-century Frankfurt. Tip: check the website for opening hours and consider a combined ticket with the nearby Goethe Museum.

signature.name: St. Paul's Church
signature.detail: A historic church that served as the seat of the first German National Assembly in 1848, making it a symbol of German democracy. It is a must-see for history buffs. Tip: entry is free, but donations are welcome; climb the tower for a view over the city center.

signature.name: Palmengarten
signature.detail: A vast botanical garden with exotic plants from around the world, perfect for a relaxing stroll. It is one of Germany's most beautiful gardens. Tip: visit on a weekday for fewer crowds and check for seasonal exhibitions.

signature.name: Alte Oper
signature.detail: A grand concert hall that was rebuilt after World War II, hosting world-class performances. Its architecture and history make it a cultural landmark. Tip: book tickets in advance for evening concerts, and dress smartly for the occasion.

signature.name: Zoo Frankfurt
signature.detail: One of the oldest and most famous zoos in Germany, home to a wide variety of animals including rare species. It is a great attraction for families. Tip: buy tickets online to skip the queue and arrive early to see the animals at their most active.
